messages:
sam: Observability spike: 2.4k reconnects/min for streaming clients starting ~03:12 UTC. Clients report 'socket closed' then hammering reconnects.
anya: Server-side shows a matching drop in active WS count but no error logs. Weird gap between HTTP teardown and runtime close.
deploy-bot: Deploy: routing/stream-coalesce v2 -> canary at 03:10 UTC (config flag stream.coalesce=true).
sourav: That canary toggles chunk buffering to reduce upstream write syscalls. We thought it was harmless.
anya: Hypothesis: coalescing makes some intermediate proxies see a zero-length flush and reply 204/200 early, so client sees connection close while our runtime still has session.
natalie: If proxy returns a synthetic early response we can get half-close state: client reconnects, then server later finishes and we end up double-charging tokens.
atalie: We need two things immediately: (1) stop the canary, (2) surface app-level heartbeat and server-close events in console so ops can distinguish benign keepalive from application frame activity.
sam: Agreed. Hotfix: roll back stream.coalesce -> false. I'll patch the canary now.
corey: For longer term: add X-App-Heartbeat header or embedded 'hb' frames that increment a monotonic counter. Console can show last_hb and hb_streak.
sourav: We should also change billing semantics: don't count tokens on pure heartbeat frames. Only bill on non-heartbeat content tokens.
anya: That will reduce duplicate billing when the server finishes after client already reconnected. But we still need a session-reattach protocol: if client reconnects within 8s with same session_id, reattach and reconcile billing.
atalie: UX/console side: add a 'reconnect-churn' panel, percent reattaches vs fresh sessions, and a breadcrumb trace linking routing config flips to churn spikes.
corey: Also instrument rollouts: every routing config change should emit a rollout_tag in the stream telemetry so historical dashboards can correlate. Right now we only have infra tags at host-level.
sourav: Implementation concerns: heartbeat frames increase token counts if not careful and might change batching heuristics. We'll need to treat hb as zero-cost and exclude from batching triggers.
sam: Test plan: (A) simulate proxy early-204 by returning empty body mid-stream; (B) simulate client tab-suspend/browser throttle that pauses frames; (C) validate session reattach logic with race windows. Add these to runtime integration tests.
natalie: Product/entitlement note: session-reattach semantics are fine for Hosted but Dedicated/Private customers may want opt-out; add tenant-level config.
corey: SDK change: expose onclose.reason with server_close_code and server_suggested_backoff. Clients should honor suggested_backoff before reconnecting.
anya: Console alerting: trigger when reconnect-churn > baseline + 20% for 3m and when reattach_rate < 80% (indicates double-new sessions).
atalie: Roadmap estimate: hotfix today, heartbeat + session-reattach + billing change = 2 sprints, console panels + rollout tagging = 1 sprint.
sam: Rolling back canary now. Will post status update in 5m.
deploy-bot: Rollback executed: routing/stream-coalesce -> false on canary cluster at 03:18 UTC.
sourav: After rollback I see reconnects drop to steady-state in canary. Good sign.
natalie: I'll file console tickets and own the dashboard work. corey can you handle SDK doc updates?
corey: Yep, I'll draft SDK guidance and a small client helper for reattach.
anya: I'll start the runtime PR for heartbeat frames and zero-cost markings. Need reviewers from serving and billing.
sam: Thanks team. Follow-ups: add tests, rollout policy per-tenant, and update billing docs. If churn pops back up after rollback, re-escalate. :white_check_mark:
